I've found this peculiar little tool at home, hidden among other odds. Not a particularly exciting object—just something you’d expect from any household with the tidierness of my parents'. I’ve always admired their way with organizing the kitchen drawers: a spoon here, two cups over yesteryonder. I’m the one who tends the bathroom cabinet, where a myriad collection has gathered like dust. 

This tool, then—it’s an ordinary rubber-banded paper towel dispenser, with its usual role to serve the daily needs in my home: dispensation. And suddenly there it lay—something that, to all outward senses—looks no better or differently today from what was before.

What made the ordinary different is what it does: it has this small notch in between two pricks where I could clip it on my wrist for handy use when needed
